messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: getAverageLog
parts:
Hi,

I am using getAverageLog to do various summaries per probe across
samples. For example,

rowMax<-function(mat,na.rm=TRUE){apply(mat,1,max,na.rm=na.rm)}
maxNMoOnHu_HM<-getAverageLog(csNMoOnHu_HM,mean=rowMax,prefix="maxInt",verbose=-1)

My problem/question is that this creates a cel file with a bunch of
stuff behind it, for example
.maxInt-intensities-customMean-mad,af6630d2b8090558ab05dfdcabc6faf1.CEL

If I want to come back to this value without recomputing it, how do I do
this? (when I reran the code above, on one set of arrays it just grabbed
the existing one and on another set it recalculated so I have two cel
files now). Should I just copy that name and grab it as a cel file by
its file name, or is there a nicer way to do this?

Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] getAverageLog
parts:
Hi Elizabeth,

the design is such that you should never have specify the specific
pathname of internal files like those. Those files containing
"average" estimates should be considered internal and
temporary/redundant (because they hold the average of the main set).

The getAverageLog() calls getAverageFile(). In your case I guess your
'csNMoOnHu' is a regular AffymetrixCelSet, so the method of interest
is getAverageFile.AffymetrixCelSet(). The tag
'af6630d2b8090558ab05dfdcabc6faf1' is a hexadecimal MD5 hashcode
generated from a set of key objects that should make the tag unique
given the input data and the getAverageFile() arguments. For
instance, if you drop one array or change a preprocessing step, that
ID tag will change. Thus, if nothing changed, the ID tag should be
the same for the same input (between R sessions and computers).

However, although getAverageFile() takes other values of argument
'mean' than the default "mean" and "median", e.g. function rowMax() in
your case, the code has only been thoroughly tested for the former.
So, that your ID tag changes although you pass the same input, might
be a bug. But before troubleshooting, are you 100% sure you didn't
change anything? The ID tag is currently generated from the key set:

key <- list(method="getAverageFile", class=class(this)[1],
arrays=sort(getNames(this)), mean=meanName, sd=sdName);

where 'meanName' and 'sdName' equals argument "customMean" and
"customSd" in your case. In this case, I really suspect that
something changed in your array names.

As you see from the above code (and the source code), regardless of
what custom 'mean' function you pass, it will be named the same, i.e.
"customMean". This is *not* safe/good, because it will generate the
same set of keys and hence the same set of ID tag if you change
mean=rowMax to say mean=rowMin. Please be aware of this. Note, there
are no such problems if you specify one of the default 'mean' or 'sd'
values. I've noticed that you specifying argument 'prefix', which is
added to the filename so it protects against this as long as you
change the prefix with your custom 'mean' - was this your reason?

Finally, I also sometimes end up with two or more "average" files,
e.g. when I rename one of the array files. That's ok and you can
safely ignore that extract "average" file (or just delete it; look at
the timestamp).

Hope this helps

Henrik
